title: Cloudflare control-plane data-center power failure
source_title: Post mortem on the Cloudflare Control Plane and Analytics Outage
alert: Cloudflare control-plane and analytics functions became unavailable after a power incident in a core data center. Investigate the dependency failure and documented disaster-recovery decision.

evidence.text: One utility power feed to PDX-DC04 was interrupted by maintenance; generators supplemented the remaining feed.
A subsequent ground fault took down facility power sources; UPS batteries ran out before power was restored. Details of the electrical root trigger were not fully verified.
evidence.source_section: Informed Speculation On What Happened Next

evidence.text: Cloudflare lost reachability to routers at its major Oregon site; control-plane and analytics services degraded.
Critical dependencies including Kafka and ClickHouse remained tied to the affected facility, despite high-availability expectations.
evidence.source_section: Designing for Data Center Level Failure

evidence.text: Cloudflare decided to fail over remaining impacted control-plane services to European disaster recovery sites.
Most relocated control-plane services were stable, while some logging and specialized services remained impaired.
All services were eventually restored; customer data-plane traffic had continued to work.

impact_options.name: Customer traffic through the global data plane

root_hypotheses.description: A facility-wide power failure at PDX-DC04 exposed insufficiently isolated control-plane and analytics dependencies
A global customer traffic WAF regex issue
A massive internet-wide DNS hijacking attack

response_options.description: Activate disaster recovery for affected control-plane services while separately restoring the power-affected facility
Shut down all global data-plane points of presence
Force every customer to rotate API credentials

dataset_origin: Published first-party incident postmortem; curated and paraphrased source facts (NOT original telemetry)
